english.title: Send thing to prison to assist escape
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) with intent to facilitate the escape of **(..SPECIFY NAME..), a prisoner in

(A)_[His Majesty's prison at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..),]_
(B)_[His Majesty's remand centre at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..) being an institution to which section 43 of the Prison Act 1952 applied,]_
(C)_[His Majesty's young offenders institution at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..) being an institution to which section 43 of the Prison Act 1952 applied,]_
(D)_[His Majesty's secure training centre at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..) being an institution to which section 43 of the Prison Act 1952 applied,]_

sent (by post or otherwise) **(..SPECIFY ITEM(S)..)

(E)_[into the said prison]_
(F)_[into the said remand centre]_
(G)_[into the said young offenders institution]_
(H)_[into the said secure training centre]_
(I)_[to a prisoner]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 39 of the Prison Act 1952.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This Standard Offence Wording is obsolete as from 31st March 2008. Repealed by the Offender Management Act 2007.
(ii) Provisions relating to charges under this section and particularly the meaning of the word 'prison' must be construed strictly. See section 42 and section 43(5) of the Prison Act 1952.
(iii) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.

Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment.
